sections.html:
Anderson sits in the northwest corner of South Carolina as the Anderson County seat, about halfway along the Interstate 85 corridor between Atlanta and Charlotte. The city had 28,106 residents in 11,282 households in 2020, and 31,323 are estimated for 2025. The median age is 36.6.

Those numbers cover only the city limits. The county is far bigger, and a house just outside the line may follow different rules. Factories lead the economy, with Glen Raven, AnMed and a large Upstate supplier base among the employers, so an owner transferred for work may not want a long listing period.

The Electric City nickname comes from an early power plant, and much of the housing dates from that era. Buyers want to hear how old the wiring, plumbing and roof are. With about 50 inches of rain a year, look at the roof, the gutters and the crawl space yourself before an inspector does.

The City of Anderson enforces nuisance rules for excessive weeds and grass, debris in yards, substandard and dilapidated housing, and abandoned vehicles. To report a violation, call (864) 231-2217 or use the Request Service button on the city website.

A case moves in stages and takes about 4 to 6 weeks:

  1. A courtesy summons goes to the owner, tenant or person in charge. The case closes if the problem is fixed within 14 days.
  2. If the problem remains, the Building Department sends a Uniform Ordinance Summons and sets a hearing at least 10 days after service.
  3. For owners who can't be found or who live outside the city, certified mail is used and hearings are set at least 30 days out.

When nobody can be served in person, the summons goes on the property and into the mail to the owner named in the tax records. A seller who lives elsewhere can miss a notice for weeks, which is why the county needs your current mailing address.

sections.h2: Permits and fees before you sell
sections.html:
Permits are needed for new construction, repairs and renovations: building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, demolition and sign. The city takes applications through its ViewPoint Cloud portal, and a contractor must hold a state license and a city business license.

The fee schedule effective July 1, 2022 holds two items that sellers should know. Work begun without a permit costs a $200 fine plus a doubled permit fee, and each re-inspection costs $50. Building and Codes is at (864) 231-2217. Confirm the street address before you go, since the department's listing is the Municipal Business Center, 601 S. Main St.

Fixing a house to list it the usual way means permits, inspections and contractor time. A cash sale as is avoids those steps for the seller.

A written property condition disclosure statement goes to the buyer in most sales of homes with one to four units. Both sides may sign an agreement to skip it, and selling as is is allowed. Knowingly false or incomplete answers can make a seller liable for damages and costs.

A South Carolina attorney must supervise the closing, because the State Bar treats drafting, closing and recording as the practice of law. Deeds are recorded at 401 East River Street with the Anderson County Register of Deeds, which serves the public weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Documents are due by 4:30 p.m.

Recording costs $1.85 per $500 of the price under state law, and $0.55 of that goes to the county. Free fraud alerts are offered by the register, and property records can be searched on the county's ACPASS site.

sections.h2: Property tax when an Anderson house is sold
sections.html:
Bills can be paid from September 30 to January 15. Late charges run 3 percent on January 16, 7 percent more after the second day of February and 5 percent more after March 17. Selling triggers reappraisal, and the 4 percent rate on an owner-occupied home applies only if the owner applied.

Unpaid tax comes out of the sale proceeds, and the closing attorney arranges the payoff. Office details are in our Anderson County tax guide.

sections.h2: Preparing for a fast Anderson sale
sections.html:
First learn what the city and county already have on your house. Ask Building and Codes about open cases, confirm the county's mailing address for you and request a tax payoff. A surprise in any of the three can delay closing by weeks.

After that, choose between a standard listing and a cash sale. Listing means permits for repairs, inspections and a buyer's lender. In a cash sale the buyer accepts the house in its present state, while the attorney still deals with the disclosure choice, the deed and the tax payoff.

Bring the closing attorney in early either way, and keep a copy of every notice you get.

sections.h2: If you live out of town
sections.html:
Owners who live far away are the likeliest to be caught off guard, since notices follow the address on the tax records. Anyone who inherited a house or moved away should update the county and ask a neighbor or property manager to watch for a posting on the door.

When a summons can't be served in person, the city posts it and mails it, and certified mail is used for owners outside the city, with hearings at least 30 days out. A missed hearing date can turn a small grass problem into a longer case, which then shows up when a buyer's title search runs.

Your attorney drafts the deed, checks title and lines up payoffs. Once you sign, the deed is taken to the Register of Deeds on East River Street, where the 4:30 p.m. cutoff means a late afternoon filing waits for the next day.

Settle with the attorney before closing who covers the recording fee. The contract decides, and the figure is the state's $1.85 per $500 of price. The free fraud alerts are worth setting up if you will keep other property in the county.

Keep a copy of the recorded deed.

sections.h2: Staying ahead of a code case
sections.html:
The simplest way to avoid a hearing is to clear the problem inside the 14 days a courtesy summons allows. Cut the grass and weeds, haul off debris and move or remove any abandoned vehicle. If the house is dilapidated and repairs are out of reach, tell the Building Department what you plan to do, since a documented plan reads better than silence.

Report a neighbor's problem the same way: call (864) 231-2217 or use Request Service on the city website. When you sell, a clean record means the buyer's title search finds nothing to hold up the closing.

faqs.q: Why is Anderson, SC called the Electric City?
faqs.a: Power arrived in 1895 from a Rocky River hydroelectric plant, early for the Southeast, and the city was first in the world to run a cotton gin on electricity.

faqs.q: How many people live in Anderson, SC?
faqs.a: There were 28,106 in 2020, and about 31,323 are estimated for 2025.

faqs.q: What happens if the city cites my Anderson house for overgrown grass or debris?
faqs.a: You first get a courtesy summons with 14 days to fix it. If the problem remains, a Uniform Ordinance Summons follows and a hearing is set, and the whole process takes about 4 to 6 weeks.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Anderson house as is?
faqs.a: Yes, state law permits it. The disclosure statement is still due unless both sides sign off in writing, and an attorney supervises the closing.

faqs.q: Where do I find Anderson County property records?
faqs.a: Try the Register of Deeds, 401 East River Street, (864) 260-4054, or search ACPASS online.
